text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH

- Wives of delgates in the conservative True Path Party are putting pressure on thier husbands to halt their support for party leader and deputy prime minister Tansu Ciller. Delegates' wives had been instrumental in her election as party leader in 1993.

- Building has begun on a natural gas pipeline between Turkey and Iran. The natural gas deal with Iran, signed by Islamist Prime Minister Necemetin Erbakan, had angered Turkey's ally, the United States.
MILLIYET
- Four opposition parties agreed on a censure motion to topple the Islamist-led government and will submit the motion to parliament on Friday.
- The ICC coal mining company will begin to work at full capacity using technology it developed itself.
HURRIYET
- Tycoon Sakip Sabanci said he could take a role in governing the country for a limited period, hinting that he may be about to enter politics.

- The head of the Turkish desk of the International Monetary Fund, Martin Hardy, says money raised from "suitcase trading" cannot be over $2 billion. Turkey has said the figure was around $8 and $9 billion.
YENI YUZYIL
- Ciller has turned down a call from her own party dissident Yalim Erez to pull out of its ruling coalition with Islamists.
RADIKAL

- The manager of the internationally-known investment fund Templeton, Mark Mobius, said foreign investers are fleeing the Turkish stock market because they are afraid of a growing Islamist movement in the country.
CUMHURIYET
- The members of a court studying a case that may lead to the closure of the Islamist Welfare Party -- the senior coalition party -- say they are threathened by Islamists.
- Turkey's state-owned Emlak Bank is carrying out research to determine whether Turkish Cyprus is a convienient place in which to invest in residential sites.
DUNYA
- The government will lift current taxes on petroluem and its products, but plans to replace them with a new special tax.
ZAMAN
- The general secretary of the military-dominated National Security Council has appointed officers to inspect some private schools.
- Pensioners will be paid their pensions on time at last as banks have prepared the payments a week ahead. Many pensioners could not get their pensions last time.
